recipes.name: Sensational Chicken Noodle Soup
ingredients_raw: 4 cups Swanson® Chicken Broth or Swanson® Certified Organic Chicken Broth or Swanson® Natural Goodness® Chicken Broth
1 cup shredded cooked chicken or turkey

steps.text: Bring broth, carrot, celery, and generous dash black pepper to a boil in a 2-quart saucepan over medium-high heat.
Stir in chicken and noodles; reduce heat to medium. Cook until noodles are tender, 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

raw_recipe.headline: Sensational Chicken Noodle Soup
raw_recipe.description: This sensational chicken noodle soup recipe requires only six ingredients—chicken broth, chicken or turkey, carrots, celery, egg noodles, and pepper.

review.reviewBody: this recipe rocks!! I alredy my it 12 times this month!! I also added

I loved this recipe for its simplicity but I did alter it a bit. First I boiled three thin chicken breasts for 30 minutes. I sauteed the carrots and celery in a quarter cup of butter. I used two carrots and three celery hearts. I put the celery leaves aside, chopped them up for later. After I sauteed the veggies, I doubled the amount of broth and used two containers of Swanson broth. I threw the carrots and celery in a pot with the broth along with the chopped celery leaves, added a pinch of salt, a pinch of ground pepper, a quarter teaspoon of oregano and a couple sprinkles of garlic powder. Brought that to a boil, added 10 oz of egg noodles and cooked that for 10 minutes covered.

While this was happening, I cut up the chicken that I had put aside into shredded cubes. Threw the chicken in at the very end and voila. I cannot put onions in my food which is a drag but my boyfriend loathes them so I deal lol. It came out delicious. My slider door was opening and the neighbor's cat was going nuts for the smell trying to get in haha. I will definitely make it again but I may even triple the broth or add less noodles as it was a very hearty soup.

Having a hubby on the couch with a cold, I looked this up. It was a good start. I like how I enhanced it: two chicken breasts, which I simmered in about 5 c. water for a half-hour. Removing them to dice them up, I added about 1 T of minced garlic, a few handfulls of angelhair pasta, a few large pinches of dried parsley, and a few large pinches of oregano. I added the recommended Mrs. Dash's, which gave it a lot more zip. I also grated some mini-carrots (about 8), and let them simmer with the broth for about 10 min., before I added the diced-up chicken. Salt and pepper to taste. It was really yummy, and became 5-star!

My husband had a cold and felt lousy. I needed something fast and comforting. This
was perfect. Nothing fancy just a good base recipe to which you can add your own
spin. Leftover chicken broth and chopped chicken in my freezer--check, leftover peas in the freezer--check, love onions-chopped 1/2 onion and thinly sliced some baby carrots. No celery--used celery salt instead, perfect. Needed additional broth so I used instant chicken bouillon. Threw in extra noodles. Lunch in 25 minutes!

The recipe was wonderful! I made enough for 12 servings to make sure we had leftovers. I used part chicken broth and part chicken stock. I boiled some dark and some white meat chicken and shredded it. Shredding gave it more of a home-style texture. Once the chicken was done boiling I added some shredded carrot, celery, parsley, and some salt and pepper. I boiled it then strained out the vegetables. This was also added to the liquid. The extra liquid was great because once the noodles went in, they sucked up a lot. With the vegetables I added a whole onion and some minced garlic. My boyfriend had a pretty bad cold so he added some habanero flakes to his bowl to kick up the heat and clear him up a bit. It was really good if you can handle spicy foods. I will definitely make this again.

Without my few additions, it is a little bland. Still good, though, so three stars for the original recipe. I added half an onion, minced, minced garlic, and plenty of basil. I threw the veggies, onion, and garlic in the pot with some unsalted butter and cooked it for about five minutes, then added the broth and seasonings and followed the rest of the recipe exactly. With these changes it gets four stars, easily. I will certainly be making this again.

Used chicken thighs + rosemary, thyme and garlic to make the stock. 35mins, and removed meat, and simmered bones etc for further 40mins letting stock reduce. Used root veggies, but, used soup-pasta instead of rice, and added the chicken meat 10mins prior to serving. Enough soup for dinner 2 nights running (2nd day's soup even better) + a further 3 portions in the freezer. Love the app and the input from all various contributors
I used may own turkey stock made from leftover carcass, added salt and topped with torn fresh Italian parsley leaves. I made 10 servings and it made 4 to 5 dinner-sized soup bowls.

This is a great BASE recipe if you need to know proportions for meat, noodles, veggies and broth. After you have that, you can double... and of course you can add more kinds of veggies (we did onions, carrots and celery) and played with favorite spices and seasonings. Thanks for giving a great jumping board!

I should add we had to add extra noodles. Also salt. And added: Garlic power, thyme, 2 bay leaves, ground pepper.

This is such an awesome quick and easy soup. I added some onion an sauteed all of my veggies in a little butter to start, then added the broth an brought to a boil. I used leftover turkey for the meat, an bow tie pasta since that is what I had on hand, 1/2 cup did not seem like enough so I bumped to 1 cup. I seasoned with a little salt & lots of pepper also added some fresh flat leaf parsley since I had some. OH! I did add two 1/4 teaspoons of garlic powder since I didn't have any garlic cloves. 1/4 tsp of garlic powder is the equivalent to one garlic clove. Just thought I would throw that little tip out there. This soup is a must try. I will be making this again and next time I think I will even add in some frozen green peas.
I added onion and sautéed the veggies before adding broth. I doubled the recipe and doubled the noodles with NoYolks dumplings. Great comfort food for the common cold!
I made this vegan style by substituting vegan chicken and vegetable broth. It was delicious!
Quick, easy, great lunch prep. Freezes well too.

Yum! This is a great jumping off point to make soup. I had all sorts of Thanksgiving leftovers so any veggies and turkey I had I put in here. Using the Swanson broth makes it so easy! Just finished my first bowl and it was delicious!
Definitely more broth otherwise it was great. Super easy to make.
Fantastic. Great flavor. Easy and delicious.

Delicious! I made some modifications. I doubled the chicken and added a cup or more of noodles. I like a thick soup. I used sodium free chicken stock so I could add salt to my taste. It is an easy and tasty soup.

Great easy recipe! The only changes I made were 1) I used Penzeys Mural of Flavor instead of straight black pepper and 2) I added more noodles (preference). My whole family liked it. Thanks for posting! Will definitely make again.
Amazing in it’s simplicity. No need to add or change a thing!
Really, really good. I added some seasonings based on other reviews. It's an easy recipe for people like me who hate to cook.
